label: highlight
text: Our p99 regression turned out to be Nagle's algorithm interacting with delayed ACKs on a new gRPC proxy: 40ms stalls on small writes. Setting TCP_NODELAY on the upstream socket fixed it. If you see suspiciously exact 40ms latencies, look here first.

label: highlight
text: I read 40 postmortems from the last two years. 'Human error' was cited as root cause in 28, but in 22 of those the same change had been made safely many times before; the differentiator was a missing guardrail, not the person. Blameless isn't a nicety, it's how you find the guardrail.

label: highlight
text: 'AI will replace radiologists' ignored that imaging volume grew faster than automation. Radiologist employment rose after 2016 because cheaper reads increased demand. The accurate worry is about task mix and pay, not headcount.

label: highlight
text: LLM-as-judge correlated about 0.8 with humans on style but only about 0.5 on factual correctness in our tests (n=600). We now use judges for tone and humans or programmatic checks for facts.

label: highlight
text: The 'wealth effect' is weaker than commonly assumed: estimates put the marginal propensity to consume out of housing wealth at roughly 2-5 cents per dollar. That's why equity rallies lift spending only modestly, and why the main transmission channel for rate changes is credit availability.

label: highlight
text: Rawls' veil of ignorance is often used to defend redistribution, but it also embeds risk-attitude assumptions. If people are less risk-averse than he assumes, the same device can license inequality. The argument's force comes from the premise, not the device.

text: We stopped quarterly OKR scoring. Teams were sandbagging targets to score green. Now we review 'what did we learn that changed a plan'. Planning time dropped 40% and surprise misses became visible about six weeks earlier.

label: highlight
text: The reproducibility problem in psychology is real, but 'half of studies are wrong' overstates it. The large replication projects found roughly 40-60% success depending on criteria, with effects about half the original size. The better lesson: treat single studies as noisy estimates and weigh pre-registered ones more.

label: highlight
text: Ranked-choice voting doesn't produce moderates as often as claimed. Evidence from Alaska and Maine shows modest shifts; candidate positions respond more to primary structure and campaign finance than to ballot format. Turnout effects were negligible in the studies I've seen.

label: highlight
text: I think open-sourcing model weights is net-positive today, but the argument won't hold forever. The key variable is marginal uplift on dangerous capabilities relative to what search already provides. Today uplift is small; if evals show it growing, release norms should flip. We should agree on that trigger in advance.

label: highlight
text: Counterintuitive: adding a cache made our system slower. Hit rate was 12%, but every miss paid serialization plus a network hop. Removing it cut p50 by 9ms. Measure hit rate before you celebrate.

label: highlight
text: I'm pessimistic about AI agents handling procurement soon. In three pilots agents succeeded on 70% of well-specified purchase tasks, but the failures were silent: wrong supplier mapped, wrong unit. A 30% failure rate with no error signal costs more than doing it by hand. Detection, not capability, is the blocker.

label: highlight
text: Summary of the sparse-autoencoder interpretability work: features can be causally steered, e.g. amplifying one feature changes outputs in predictable ways. Limitations: coverage is partial, and reconstruction loss means some computation isn't captured. It's evidence that interpretability is tractable, not proof of full understanding.
